name: Thang Tam communal house
summary: The fishermen’s communal house and whale hall: see the whale skeleton, or come for the whale festival. The hall dates from Minh Mạng’s reign, 1820–1840. On an ordinary day the visit is the buildings and the bones. The Nghinh Ông festival falls on the 16th of the 8th lunar month.
getThere: 104 Hoàng Hoa Thám, inland from Back Beach.
heroCaption: Whale bones kept in the hall at Thang Tam

notice.title: The procession is one morning a year
notice.body: The boats leave Front Beach at dawn on the 16th of the 8th lunar month, and the solar date changes each year. On other days there is no procession.

body: Đình Thắng Tam was built under Emperor Minh Mạng, 1820–1840. The whale is worshipped here as Nam Hải, alongside Thiên Y A Na and other sea spirits. The complex holds the communal house, the whale hall, and Miếu Bà.

On an ordinary day you see the buildings and the whale skeleton kept in the hall. For the ritual, come for Nghinh Ông: boats leave Front Beach at dawn and sail toward Hòn Bà, then a palanquin is carried inland along Quang Trung, Trương Công Định, and Hoàng Hoa Thám to the hall. In 2026 the public days were 26 and 27 September, with offerings and hát bội opera in the hall.

figures.caption: The whale model kept with the hall on Hoàng Hoa Thám
figures.alt: A whale model inside the Thang Tam whale hall in Vung Tau

gettingThere: The hall is at 104 Hoàng Hoa Thám, the street that runs inland from Back Beach.

legs.heading: From Back Beach
legs.body: Walk or ride up Hoàng Hoa Thám from the beach road.

legs.heading: From Front Beach
legs.body: Taxi across town by Quang Trung and Hoàng Hoa Thám, the festival route.
